'''Janice B. Walker''' is an American mathematician who taught and served as an administrator at [[Xavier University]] in Cincinnati and Assistant to the President and Chief Diversity and Inclusion Officer there.

==Biography==
Janice Anita Brown Walker<ref name=":1">Walker, Janice Anita Brown. ''Closure and Expansions in Series of Complex Exponentials''. University of Michigan, 1982.</ref> was born in [[Meridian, Mississippi]], and raised in Florida.<ref name=":0" /> She earned her BS in mathematics at [[Tuskegee University]] and her MA and Ph.D. in mathematics at the [[University of Michigan|University of Michigan - Ann Arbor]] (1982). The title of her dissertation was ''Closure and Expansions in Series of Complex Exponentials'' and her advisor was Douglas Grassel Dickson.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Janice B. Walker - Black Women in Mathematics |url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/walker_janice_b.html |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Janice Walker - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=7089 |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

Before earning her Ph.D., Walker held several University of Michigan positions in Ann Arbor. In 1982, Walker moved to [[Cincinnati]], Ohio to become an assistant professor at Xavier University. In 1986, she was named associate professor, and beginning in 1992, she served as chair of the Mathematics and Computer Science department for seven years. In 1999, she became dean of the College of Arts and Sciences and served for 17 years.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Network-Ohio |first=ACE Women's |title=Dr. Janice Walker (2016) |url=https://www.aceohiowomen.org/plugins/content/content.php?content.220 |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=www.aceohiowomen.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Board |url=https://www.breakthroughcincinnati.org/about/board |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=Breakthrough Cincinnati |language=en-US}}</ref>

Walker was Xavier's vice president for Institutional Diversity and Inclusion for five years after which she rejoined the mathematics department before retiring from the university.<ref name=":3" />

In 2019, Walker contributed to Xavier's purchase of ten works of art for an exhibit titled, “Art at the X: Celebrating Women,” which was staged along with the university's 50th anniversary of the admission of women as traditional day students. The ten pieces were later added to the university's permanent art collection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Art at the X: Celebrating Women |url=https://www.xavier.edu/now/2019/cas-newsletter-fall-2019/art-at-x |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=Xavier University |language=en}}</ref>

Walker retired from Xavier in 2022. She serves as a board member of Breakthrough Cincinnati and other community organizations.<ref name=":3" />
